mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% over the prior quarter is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite sustained FEDFUNDS > 4% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer pay growth (HOUST) create a labor market softening that precedes S&P 500 declines over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases over the prior 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) when the interaction signal is inverted.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in retail sales (not available in the catalog) would drive S&P 500 gains over the next 5 days, but since we cannot proxy retail sales, this sketch is omitted.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns show no correlation with GDPC1 growth (Pearson's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% while inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 5% suggests supply-side strength that supports S&P 500 gains over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > 2% and CPIAUCSL < 5% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the interaction signal remaining above 0.5 in a 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 0.5% while the Federal Funds rate remains steady, it indicates persistent inflationary pressure that is associated with negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) when the CPIAUCSL change is <= 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months triggers a wage growth cycle that supports S&P 500 gains over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no correlation with UNRATE trend (Spearman's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising home sales proxies (not available) would predict S&P 500 gains over 20 days, but this sketch is omitted due to missing proxies.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite GDPC1 growth above trend.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales proxies (not available) both show double-digit growth, it signals a supply boom that precedes S&P 500 5-day outperformance. (Omitted due to missing proxy.)
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns underperform the S&P 500 total market index (M2) by more than 10 basis points.
